scope: Paraphrased evidence from named retrieved publisher/author/repository material. This is not a systematic review, proof of historical priority or a new citation snapshot. Whole documents were not read unless explicitly stated; no acquired full-text files are authorized for publication by this memo.

articles.access_scope: APA publisher search-index abstract and official issue contents; direct DOI fetch robots-denied
articles.locator: Abstract and June2010 special-issue contents pp81–93
articles.contribution: Yukl and Mahsud distinguish flexible/adaptive leadership conceptions, synthesize relevant research streams and discuss practical guidance and research limitations.
articles.limit: A synthesis; the abstract explicitly does not claim a comprehensive review of every stream. This does not establish founding priority, effects of a training program or equivalence with Heifetz's framework.

articles.locator: Abstract; Leading and following as a complex adaptive process; Theoretical implications
articles.contribution: DeRue develops an interactional account in which recurring leader/follower exchanges generate identities, relationships and structures; this challenges fixed, hierarchical leader/follower categories.
articles.limit: Theoretical development, not an experimental demonstration of effectiveness or proof this is the first adaptive leadership formulation.

articles.access_scope: Publisher DOI retrieval failed. Frozen corpus abstract remains the available substantive source; external third-party summaries were not accepted as primary evidence.
articles.locator: No newly acquired primary publisher text
articles.contribution: Primary-page verification remains unavailable in this pass; any inclusion must explicitly rely on the frozen abstract and retain its two-case, higher-education scope.
articles.limit: Do not describe a successful publisher/fulltext appraisal or causal proof.

articles.access_scope: Author abstract from PubMed search-index record; direct page renderer returned only a notice
articles.contribution: Thygeson, Morrissey and Ulstad apply Heifetz's technical/adaptive distinction to clinical encounters and patients' own work of adapting.
articles.limit: Literature review and theory development; claimed promise for outcomes does not itself demonstrate clinical effectiveness.

articles.access_scope: PMC retrieved abstract, background and conceptual/research-exemplar excerpts
articles.locator: Abstract; Overview and background; conceptual measurement discussion
articles.contribution: Bailey and colleagues develop the point-of-care research use of adaptive leadership, illustrating five nursing research problems and emphasizing the need to define and measure the concepts.
articles.limit: Conceptual/research-agenda contribution, not five completed intervention-effectiveness trials.

articles.access_scope: PMC retrieved framework and discussion excerpts
articles.locator: The Adaptive Leadership Framework for Chronic Illness; collaborative-care model discussion
articles.contribution: Anderson and colleagues adapt the framework to ongoing chronic illness, emphasizing patient/family-provider relationships, changing challenges and shared care work over time.
articles.limit: Framework/research agenda; a proposed mechanism or model does not establish its clinical effects.

articles.access_scope: PMC abstract, background, implications and limitations excerpts
articles.locator: Abstract Design and Methods; discussion limitations
articles.contribution: Corazzini and colleagues examine adaptive challenges during person-directed nursing-home culture change using seven focus groups across three nursing homes.
articles.limit: Qualitative observation; progress was not benchmarked and a for-profit chain home was absent. No causal effectiveness claim or broad representativeness.

articles.access_scope: Author-provided abstract in ERIC search-index record; journal page inaccessible and direct ERIC page timed out
articles.contribution: Nelson and Squires present a conceptual discussion of adaptive leadership for collaborative problem solving with multiple stakeholders.
articles.limit: Conceptual synthesis/application, not original founding of the theory or an effectiveness trial.

articles.access_scope: Primary publisher abstract and citation metadata
articles.contribution: Xiao and colleagues study leadership functions in real trauma resuscitations using grounded-theory analysis of152 video segments from18 cases.
articles.limit: A distinct empirical team-leadership strand. It is not automatically the Heifetz conceptual framework; local citation zero is an observed-boundary finding, not evidence of no influence.

articles.access_scope: Primary journal article copy hosted by an author interest group; cover and first-article abstract inspected, not the complete40-page packet
articles.locator: PDFp1 cover award/abstracts; PDFp2 first article abstract; printedp15
articles.contribution: Glover and colleagues'2002 pair develops adaptive leadership through Piaget's assimilation/accommodation and four capacities spanning cultural competence, knowledge, diversity and vision.
articles.limit: An early distinct formulation in this selection; not proof it originated the whole field. The cover's journal award is a separate editorial recognition, not bibliometric or human review of our shortlist. Do not redistribute the PDF.

contextual_foundations.finding: Uhl-Bien, Marion and McKelvey2007 distinguish adaptive, administrative and enabling functions in a complexity leadership framework.
contextual_foundations.limit: Cited external foundation, not silently added to951; framework does not make all adaptive-leadership usages identical.

contextual_foundations.finding: Uhl-Bien and Arena2018 integrate organizational-adaptability literatures and discuss tension between innovation and production.
contextual_foundations.limit: Contextual cited work outside951; later synthesis, no first-origin claim.

contextual_foundations.finding: Leadership Without Easy Answers is a Ronald Heifetz book with copyright1994 and Harvard University Press/Belknap imprint. Its DOI corresponds to the2009-dated OpenAlex record acquired separately.
contextual_foundations.limit: Retain both exact recorded IDs/years; title/edition relationships do not license automatic identity merging or pooled citation counts.

contextual_foundations.access_scope: PubMed author-abstract/citation and HBR page-version metadata
contextual_foundations.finding: Heifetz and Laurie publication documented in1997; a2001 HBR version and2009 IEEE record remain distinct observations.
contextual_foundations.limit: No automatic pooled counts or retrospective change to the observed2009 cited record.

contextual_foundations.finding: Braun/Clarke's Using thematic analysis in psychology is a generic methodology reference, rather than an adaptive-leadership theory foundation.
contextual_foundations.limit: Metadata-based role classification; no full-text appraisal asserted.
